adrenaline.definition: Excitement and visceral exhilaration during viewing.

tension.definition: Suspense, dread, or anticipation of an uncertain outcome.

fear.definition: Fright or horror experienced, independently of horror genre membership.

perceived_threat.definition: Sense that characters face harm, including harm never shown.

romantic_feeling.definition: Romantic affection or longing evoked in the viewer.

sensuality.definition: Erotic atmosphere or sexual tension, independently of explicit sexual depiction.

warmth.definition: Affectionate, kind, or emotionally welcoming tone.

wholesomeness.definition: Reassurance through care, kindness, and emotional safety.

wonder.definition: Awe, amazement, or fascination with discovery.

pathos.definition: Acute pity, sorrow, or tragic emotional impact.

uncanniness.definition: Unease from the strangely familiar or almost natural.

catharsis.definition: Emotional release after accumulated tension or feeling.

nostalgia.definition: Longing for a remembered or imagined past evoked by the work; not release age.

hopefulness.definition: Optimistic outlook or belief in positive possibilities.

emotional_intensity.definition: Overall strength of emotional engagement, regardless of positive or negative tone.

stress.definition: Sustained pressure, discomfort, or anxiety experienced during viewing.

uplift.definition: Encouragement, joy, or improved spirits evoked.

thought_provocation.definition: Invitation to reflect on ideas, ethics, or interpretations beyond the immediate plot.

playfulness.definition: Light, mischievous, or freely inventive tone.

sentimentality.definition: Overt appeal to tender feelings and emotional attachment.

emotional_restraint.definition: Understated expression and withholding of overt emotional display.

bittersweetness.definition: Positive and painful feelings intertwined rather than merely appearing separately.

absurdity.definition: Experience of incongruity, illogic, or strangeness, whether humorous or unsettling.

escapism.definition: Immersion away from everyday concerns; not limited to fantasy settings.

wish_fulfillment.definition: Invitation to imagine desired powers, relationships, status, or ways of life.

tranquility.definition: Calm, restful or meditative feeling evoked; not merely absence of tension.

indignation.definition: Moral outrage or righteous anger evoked in the viewer; distinct from anger depicted by characters.

disgust.definition: Revulsion evoked, independently of comic gross-out, frightening threat or grotesque visual style.

overall.definition: Overall amount and strength of comedy, independently of individual humor styles.

situational.definition: Humor from circumstances, misunderstandings, and complications; no episodic-format requirement.

wit_wordplay.definition: Humor from verbal cleverness, puns, or linguistic ambiguity.

physical.definition: Humor from bodily action, slapstick, or visual physical mishaps.

cringe.definition: Humor from embarrassment or uncomfortable social situations.

absurdist.definition: Humor from nonsense, illogic, or bizarre juxtapositions.

satire.definition: Humorous critique of institutions, behavior, or social conventions.

parody.definition: Humorous imitation of a recognizable work, genre, or style.

dark.definition: Humor about death, suffering, taboo, or tragedy.

running_gags.definition: Recurring jokes whose repetition or variation creates humor.

meta.definition: Humor about storytelling, production, audiences, or the work itself.

deadpan.definition: Humor delivered with apparent seriousness or minimal emotional reaction.

gross_out.definition: Humor relying on bodily fluids, disgust, or vulgar physical material.

raunchy.definition: Sexually explicit or bawdy humor; distinct from noncomic sensuality and nonsexual gross-out humor.

crime.definition: Criminal acts and their consequences as subject matter.

mystery.definition: Uncovering an important unknown as a central concern.

war.definition: Armed conflict and its human or societal consequences.

politics.definition: Governance, political institutions, and struggles for political power.

radicalization.definition: A process of adopting increasingly extreme ideological commitments or endorsing extremist action. Distinct from existing political beliefs, ordinary persuasion, rebellion, group secrecy, and coercive group control; those alone do not establish radicalization.

family.definition: Family bonds, conflict, obligations, and belonging.

psychology.definition: Mental processes, internal conflict, or perception as subject matter.

entertainment_industry.definition: The business and practice of entertainment and celebrity.

social_critique.definition: Examination or criticism of social arrangements and norms.

class.definition: Social class, economic inequality, and mobility.

capitalism.definition: Economic systems organized around capital, profit, and ownership.

consumerism.definition: Exploration or critique of acquiring goods, consumption, brands, or possessions as a source of identity, status, or fulfillment. Distinct from capitalism as an economic system; buying or using a product alone is insufficient.

technological_change.definition: Exploration of societal or personal effects of technological development, adoption, or displacement, including effects on work, relationships, institutions, and identity. Gadget presence, advanced technology, or science alone is insufficient.

human_nature.definition: Explicit thematic exploration of what humans are like: capacities, impulses, morality, cooperation, cruelty, or tensions between nature and social conditioning. Ordinary human characters, emotion, or drama alone is insufficient; not a synonym for personal identity, consciousness, or existential meaning.

faith_and_spirituality.definition: Religious belief, spiritual practice, or metaphysical meaning.

business.definition: Commercial organizations, enterprise, and work decisions.

finance.definition: Money management, financial systems, investing, or debt.

environment.definition: Relationships between human activity and ecosystems.

science.definition: Scientific inquiry and its ideas, practice, or consequences.

popular_culture.definition: Popular media, celebrity, fandom, or shared cultural trends.

survival.definition: Meeting essential needs or overcoming threats to continued life.

adventure.definition: Exploration, risk, and discovery outside ordinary life.

hacking.definition: Intrusion into or manipulation of computer systems.

artificial_intelligence.definition: Artificial agents and their interaction with the world.

consciousness.definition: The nature of subjective experience and personhood.

identity.definition: Formation, discovery, concealment, or change of personal identity.

existential_meaning.definition: Purpose, freedom, mortality, and the meaning of existence.

trauma.definition: Lasting effects of overwhelming or harmful experiences.

recovery.definition: Processes of rebuilding after trauma, illness, or crisis.

mental_health.definition: Mental health conditions, care, and lived experience.

addiction.definition: Dependency and its effects on people and relationships.

addiction_recovery.definition: Attempts to overcome dependency and maintain recovery.

trust_and_betrayal.definition: Reliance on others, deception, and broken trust.

coming_of_age.definition: Development toward adult identity, agency, or responsibility.

coming_out.definition: Disclosure or recognition of LGBTQ identity in a social context.

sexuality.definition: Sexual identity, desire, and their social meaning.

gender_identity.definition: Gender identity and its personal or social implications. Distinct from social expectations about gender roles and from sexism; do not infer identity from conformity to or rejection of a role.

gender_roles.definition: Exploration of social expectations, norms, or performances of masculinity, femininity, and gendered roles. Distinct from a person's gender identity and from sexism as discrimination; either may coexist without implying the other.

immigration.definition: Migration across borders and the experience of settlement.

displacement.definition: Loss of home or community through conflict, coercion, or other forces.

gentrification.definition: Neighborhood change associated with investment and displacement.

surveillance.definition: Monitoring, privacy, and control through observation.

disease_and_pandemics.definition: Population-level disease transmission, epidemics, pandemics or public-health response matter as subjects. Personal diagnosis, dying and care are assessed separately as illness_and_dying.

climate_change.definition: Climate processes, human causes, or consequences.

inherited_wealth.definition: Inheritance, dynastic wealth, and intergenerational economic advantage.

social_media.definition: Online social platforms and their effects on life.

public_shaming.definition: Public condemnation, reputational punishment, or social exclusion.

forgiveness.definition: Letting go of blame or reconciling after harm.

loyalty.definition: Commitment to people, groups, or principles under pressure.

belonging.definition: Acceptance, community, and finding a place among others.

loneliness.definition: Isolation and unmet desire for connection.

ambition.definition: Pursuit of achievement, status, or recognition.

labor.definition: Working conditions, worker identity, organizing, and exploitation.

colonialism.definition: Colonial domination, resistance, and its legacies.

racism.definition: Racial discrimination and its personal or structural consequences.

sexism.definition: Discrimination or domination based on sex or gender.

caregiving.definition: Responsibility for another person's everyday support and wellbeing.

parenthood.definition: Becoming or being a parent and its consequences.

aging.definition: Later life, changing capacities, and social experiences of aging.

midlife.definition: Reassessment and transitions in middle adulthood.

retirement.definition: Leaving paid work and adjusting to life afterward.

early_adulthood.definition: Independence, work, and relationships in early adult life.

artistic_creation.definition: Making art and the motivations or struggles involved.

persuasion_and_propaganda.definition: Shaping public or interpersonal belief through persuasion, spin, PR, advertising, propaganda or disinformation is a subject of the work; do not label the work itself propaganda from this score.

illness_and_dying.definition: Personal illness, diagnosis, living with illness, dying or end-of-life care is a subject; distinct from population-level epidemics.

corruption.definition: Abuse of entrusted public, organizational or professional power for private gain is a subject; not all crime or ambition is corruption.

action.definition: Genre identity organized substantially around physical action and conflict.

adventure.definition: Genre identity organized around journeys, exploration, and peril.

drama.definition: Genre identity organized around sustained human conflict and emotional development.

thriller.definition: Genre identity organized around suspense, danger, and escalating uncertainty.

horror.definition: Genre identity organized around fear, dread, or horror.

science_fiction.definition: Genre identity involving speculative science, technology, or societies.

fantasy.definition: Genre identity involving supernatural or magical premises.

romance.definition: Genre identity centered on a romantic relationship and its development.

mystery.definition: Genre identity centered on uncovering an unknown or solving a puzzle.

crime.definition: Genre identity centered on crime, criminals, or criminal investigation.

western.definition: Genre identity drawing on frontier-western conventions.

neo_western.definition: Western conventions adapted to a modern setting.

giallo.definition: Genre identity drawing on stylized Italian mystery-thriller and horror conventions.

kaiju.definition: Genre identity centered on giant monsters and their impact.

disaster.definition: Genre identity organized around a major catastrophe.

superhero.definition: Genre identity drawing on superhero narrative conventions; powers alone do not establish membership.

zombie.definition: Genre identity organized around zombies or zombie-like contagion.

slasher.definition: Horror genre identity organized around a killer stalking and attacking victims.

creature_feature.definition: Genre identity organized around encounters with threatening creatures.

neo_noir.definition: Modern use of noir conventions such as fatalism, moral ambiguity, and criminal intrigue.

space_western.definition: Combination of western conventions and a spacefaring setting.

sword_and_sorcery.definition: Fantasy adventure organized around personal peril, swordplay, and sorcery.

cozy_mystery.definition: Mystery conventions with a reassuring social setting and limited graphic menace.

romantic_comedy.definition: Romance and comedy jointly organize the work.

melodrama.definition: Genre mode built around heightened emotional conflict and expressive plotting.

musical.definition: Genre identity in which musical performance is integral to storytelling.

war.definition: Genre identity substantially organized around warfare.

historical_drama.definition: Dramatic genre identity grounded in a past historical setting.

biographical.definition: Genre identity organized around the life of a real person.

true_crime.definition: Factual treatment of actual crime; fictional crime is insufficient.

psychological_thriller.definition: Thriller conventions organized around perception, manipulation, or mental conflict.

conspiracy_thriller.definition: Thriller conventions organized around concealed coordination and institutional danger.

survival_thriller.definition: Thriller conventions organized around immediate survival under sustained threat.

legal_thriller.definition: Thriller conventions organized around legal conflict and proceedings.

police_procedural.definition: Crime conventions emphasizing investigative procedure and institutional police work.

gangster.definition: Crime conventions emphasizing organized criminal groups and their internal lives.

whodunit.definition: Mystery conventions organized around identifying who committed a crime.

puzzle_box.definition: Mystery conventions inviting reconstruction of deliberately concealed narrative rules or structure.

space_opera.definition: Science-fiction conventions emphasizing large-scale space adventure and heightened conflict.

epic_fantasy.definition: Fantasy conventions emphasizing expansive worlds, large stakes, and extended quests or conflicts.

urban_fantasy.definition: Fantasy conventions combined with a recognizably urban, usually modern social environment.

dark_fantasy.definition: Fantasy conventions combined with a threatening or macabre horror-inflected atmosphere.

investigation.definition: Characters gather evidence to explain an event or identify responsibility.

pursuit.definition: An extended chase or hunt organizes the story.

rescue.definition: Saving someone from captivity or danger organizes the story.

escape.definition: Getting out of confinement or an unsafe situation organizes the story.

quest.definition: A journey toward a defined objective organizes the story.

competition.definition: A contest with rivals and an outcome organizes the story.

relationship_development.definition: Changes in a relationship organize the story.

everyday_life.definition: Ordinary routines and small events organize the story.

survival.definition: Remaining alive under threatening conditions organizes the story.

heist.definition: Planning, carrying out, or dealing with a theft organizes the story.

espionage.definition: Secret intelligence gathering or covert state operations organize the story.

military_operation.definition: An organized military mission structures the story.

legal_case.definition: Court proceedings, formal adjudication or preparation for a legal case organize the story. Legislative debate or a political committee hearing alone belongs to political_struggle.

political_struggle.definition: Pursuit or exercise of political power structures the story.

underdog_rise.definition: An initially disadvantaged character gains standing or succeeds against stronger opposition.

revenge.definition: Retaliation for a perceived wrong drives an arc.

vigilantism.definition: Characters enforce their own justice outside formal authority.

rags_to_riches.definition: A character moves from poverty to substantial wealth.

fall_from_grace.definition: A character loses status, reputation, or moral standing.

redemption.definition: A character attempts to make amends or change after wrongdoing.

mistaken_identity.definition: A character is consequentially taken to be someone else.

memory_loss.definition: Consequential lost or inaccessible memories, missing periods of time, or inability to recall one's own actions. Includes such gaps without a clinical amnesia diagnosis; does not require permanent loss. Ordinary forgetfulness and information withheld only from the audience are insufficient.
memory_loss.presence_definition: Lost or inaccessible memories or missing periods of a character's own experience occur, whether or not diagnosed as amnesia. Ordinary forgetfulness or withholding information only from the audience is insufficient.

body_swap.definition: Characters exchange bodies or consciousness across bodies.

fish_out_of_water.definition: An unfamiliar social or physical environment challenges a character.

secret_identity.definition: Concealing an identity or maintaining a double life drives the story.

road_trip.definition: An overland journey with encounters along the way structures the story.

tournament.definition: A sequence of competitive rounds structures an arc.

training.definition: Learning or practice builds abilities toward a later challenge.

race_against_time.definition: A consequential deadline structures the conflict.

single_night.definition: The main action is concentrated in one eventful night.

locked_room.definition: An apparently inaccessible crime scene creates the central puzzle.

conspiracy.definition: Hidden coordination among powerful actors drives the plot.

apocalypse_survival.definition: Surviving societal collapse or a world-ending event drives the plot.

haunted_house.definition: An inhabited or visited dwelling is the focal site of a haunting.

chosen_one.definition: A character is singled out for a special, consequential role.

prophecy.definition: Predictions of destiny shape choices and events.

macguffin_quest.definition: Pursuit of an object whose plot function exceeds its intrinsic characterization.

final_survivor.definition: A surviving focal character confronts a threat after others are eliminated.

apparent_death.definition: A character appears to die but is later revealed to be alive.

mentor_death.definition: A mentor dies and the death matters to the mentee's arc.

doppelganger.definition: A double or lookalike produces meaningful events, identity confusion, recurring humor, or conflict. Antagonism or conflict is not required. Incidental resemblance without a narrative use is insufficient.
doppelganger.presence_definition: A double or lookalike is presented as such; incidental resemblance alone is insufficient. Conflict is not required.

hidden_antagonist_reveal.definition: A character's antagonistic role is concealed and later revealed.

home_invasion.definition: Unwanted hostile entry into a home organizes a consequential part of the story.
home_invasion.presence_definition: Whether this concept occurs within the assessed scope, independently of narrative importance: Unwanted hostile entry into a home organizes a consequential part of the story.

romantic_development.definition: Formation or deepening of a romantic relationship matters to the story.

established_couple.definition: An ongoing romantic partnership matters to the story; former partners or separated co-parents alone belong to breakup_or_divorce or parent_child.

marriage.definition: Marriage and its obligations or conflicts matter to the story.

breakup_or_divorce.definition: Ending a partnership matters to the story.

partner_bereavement.definition: Loss of a romantic partner matters to the story.

love_triangle.definition: Competing romantic attachments among three people matter to the story.

enemies_to_lovers.definition: An antagonistic relationship develops into romance.

forbidden_romance.definition: A romantic relationship faces a consequential social or institutional prohibition.

slow_burn_romance.definition: Romantic development unfolds gradually through delayed intimacy or commitment.

queer_romance.definition: An explicitly depicted LGBTQ romantic relationship matters to the story.

workplace_romance.definition: A romantic relationship between coworkers matters to the story.

age_gap_romance.definition: A substantial age difference is consequential to a romantic relationship.

friendship.definition: Non-romantic bonds of friendship matter to the story.

male_friendship.definition: Friendship among men matters to the story.

female_friendship.definition: Friendship among women matters to the story.

mentor_mentee.definition: Guidance and learning between mentor and mentee matter to the story.

student_teacher.definition: A formal educational student-teacher relationship matters to the story; no romantic implication.

rivalry.definition: Competition or mutual opposition between characters matters to the story.

forced_proximity.definition: Circumstances oblige characters to remain close or share space.

adversaries_cooperate.definition: Characters with genuinely opposing goals cooperate in a consequential shared undertaking; friendly peers in different industries are not automatically adversaries.

found_family.definition: Chosen bonds serve a family-like role in the story.

family_conflict.definition: Sustained conflict or harmful dysfunction within a family matters to the story.

intergenerational.definition: Relationships across generations matter to the story.

generational_trauma.definition: Trauma transmitted or repeated across generations matters to the story.

parent_child.definition: The relationship between parent and child matters to the story.

siblings.definition: Sibling relationships matter to the story.

caregiver_dependent.definition: Care and dependence between characters matter to the story.

human_animal_companionship.definition: An emotional bond between a person and animal matters to the story.

coercive_relationship.definition: Manipulation, coercion, or control within an interpersonal relationship matters to the story. Systematic control of members by a group is assessed separately as coercive_group_control; neither automatically implies the other.

coercive_group_control.definition: A group or leader systematically controls members through intimidation, isolation, dependency, punishment, or suppression of autonomy. Distinct from interpersonal coercion, voluntary discipline, secrecy, and radicalization; any of these may coexist but does not imply group control.
coercive_group_control.presence_definition: A group or leader systematically controls members through intimidation, isolation, dependency, punishment, or suppression of autonomy. Distinct from interpersonal coercion, voluntary discipline, secrecy, and radicalization; any of these may coexist but does not imply group control.

infidelity.definition: A breach of an agreed romantic or sexual exclusivity commitment matters to the story; consensual non-monogamy is not infidelity.
infidelity.presence_definition: Whether this concept occurs within the assessed scope, independently of narrative importance: A breach of an agreed romantic or sexual exclusivity commitment matters to the story; consensual non-monogamy is not infidelity.

unrequited_love.definition: Unreciprocated romantic attachment matters to the story.
unrequited_love.presence_definition: Whether this concept occurs within the assessed scope, independently of narrative importance: Unreciprocated romantic attachment matters to the story.

ensemble.definition: Several focal characters share narrative attention and agency.

antihero.definition: A focal character departs substantially from conventional heroic ethics or behavior.

morally_ambiguous_cast.definition: Moral ambiguity among multiple major characters matters to the work.

transformation_arc.definition: Substantial change in a focal character's beliefs, identity, or behavior.

intellectual_problem_solver.definition: A focal character's reasoning or specialized intellectual ability drives events.

detective_lead.definition: A focal character acts as an investigator or detective.

female_protagonist.definition: A woman or girl occupies a protagonist role, independently of competence or characterization quality.

child_protagonist.definition: A child occupies a protagonist role.

teen_protagonist.definition: A teenager occupies a protagonist role.

older_adult_protagonist.definition: An older adult occupies a protagonist role.

child_agency.definition: Children make consequential choices that affect events.

female_character_agency.definition: Women or girls make consequential choices that affect events.

workplace_team.definition: A team formed through work is a central social unit.

family_business.definition: A family-run business is a central social unit.

unaccompanied_children.definition: Children without their usual caregivers form a central social situation.

teen_peer_group.definition: Teenage friendships and peer-group dynamics form a central social situation.

clandestine_groups.definition: A secret society or organized group whose membership, meetings, activities, or aims are deliberately concealed. Secrecy is the defining feature, not coercion or extremist ideology; a secret held by one person, an ordinary private friendship, or crime alone is insufficient.
clandestine_groups.presence_definition: A secret society or organized group whose membership, meetings, activities, or aims are deliberately concealed. Secrecy is the defining feature, not coercion or extremist ideology; a secret held by one person, an ordinary private friendship, or crime alone is insufficient.

nonhuman_protagonist.definition: A nonhuman character occupies a protagonist role; distinguish role from production technique.
nonhuman_protagonist.presence_definition: Whether this concept occurs within the assessed scope, independently of narrative importance: A nonhuman character occupies a protagonist role; distinguish role from production technique.

solo_protagonist.definition: One protagonist carries the main narrative perspective; not a claim that there is only one cast member.
solo_protagonist.presence_definition: Whether this concept occurs within the assessed scope, independently of narrative importance: One protagonist carries the main narrative perspective; not a claim that there is only one cast member.

demonstrated_competence.definition: How consistently focal characters demonstrate effective practical, professional or intellectual skill in consequential tasks. Distinct from intelligence, claimed expertise, power, luck or training merely occurring. Zero means no demonstrated competence, not an unintelligent person. Assess the depicted performance; competence_basis separately records how skill is established.

lgbtq_characters.definition: Explicitly established LGBTQ characters have narrative importance; do not infer from allegory or creator identity.

neurodivergent_characters.definition: Explicitly established neurodivergent characters have narrative importance; do not diagnose from behavior.

disabled_characters.definition: Explicitly established disabled characters have narrative importance.

immigrant_characters.definition: Explicitly established immigrant characters have narrative importance.

advanced_technology.definition: Technology substantially beyond the work's contemporary baseline shapes its world.
advanced_technology.presence_definition: Technology substantially beyond the work's contemporary baseline occurs in its world.

magic.definition: Supernatural abilities or forces understood as magic shape the world.
magic.presence_definition: Supernatural abilities or forces understood as magic occur.

simulation.definition: An artificial simulation is an important layer of depicted reality. A physically staged real environment or social deception alone is not a simulation.
simulation.presence_definition: An artificial simulation is presented as a layer of reality.

virtual_reality.definition: Characters experience an interactive digitally mediated environment. A physical set, surveillance broadcast or deception alone is not virtual reality.
virtual_reality.presence_definition: Characters experience an interactive digitally mediated environment.

parallel_worlds.definition: Coexisting alternative realities matter to the world.

time_travel.definition: Movement across time outside ordinary chronological passage matters to the world.
time_travel.presence_definition: Movement across time outside ordinary chronological passage occurs.

travel_to_past.definition: Travel to an earlier time matters to the world.
travel_to_past.presence_definition: Travel to an earlier time occurs.

travel_to_future.definition: Travel to a later time matters to the world.
travel_to_future.presence_definition: Travel to a later time occurs.

time_loop.definition: Repetition of a period of time matters to the world or narrative.
time_loop.presence_definition: A period of time repeats within the story world.

dystopian_society.definition: Oppressive or deeply dysfunctional social arrangements define the world.
dystopian_society.presence_definition: An oppressive or deeply dysfunctional society is depicted.

post_apocalyptic.definition: Life after a civilization-scale catastrophe defines the world.
post_apocalyptic.presence_definition: Life after a civilization-scale catastrophe is depicted.

spacefaring.definition: Travel or life beyond Earth is consequential to the world.
spacefaring.presence_definition: Travel or life beyond Earth occurs.

robots.definition: Embodied artificial machines functioning as agents matter to the world; not synonymous with AI.
robots.presence_definition: Embodied artificial machines functioning as agents occur; AI without embodiment is insufficient.

myth_and_folklore.definition: Recognizable mythological or folkloric traditions shape the world.
myth_and_folklore.presence_definition: Recognizable mythological or folkloric beings, events, or practices occur in the story world; a passing idiom is insufficient.

scientific_rigor.definition: Attention to scientific constraints and explanatory consistency; not an inverse of speculative freedom.

speculative_freedom.definition: Freedom to use speculative premises without scientific elaboration.

worldbuilding_depth.definition: Detail and interconnection in the world's institutions, history, and rules.

lore_dependence.definition: Importance of remembering mythology or lore to follow the work.

magic_rule_detail.definition: Elaboration of rules and constraints governing magic.

everyday_realism.definition: Attention to plausible ordinary behavior and material conditions, independently of era.

magical_realism.definition: Impossible or supernatural events are treated as ordinary within an otherwise everyday world; distinct from an explicitly elaborated magic system.

urban.definition: A city environment is narratively important.
urban.presence_definition: A city environment is depicted as a location.

small_town.definition: A small town environment is narratively important.
small_town.presence_definition: A small town environment is depicted as a location.

rural.definition: A countryside or village environment is narratively important.
rural.presence_definition: A countryside or village environment is depicted as a location.

frontier.definition: A frontier environment is narratively important.
frontier.presence_definition: A frontier environment is depicted as a location.

polar.definition: An Arctic, Antarctic, or comparable polar environment is narratively important.
polar.presence_definition: An Arctic, Antarctic, or comparable polar environment is depicted as a location.

mountains.presence_definition: Mountain landscapes are depicted as locations.

forest.presence_definition: Woodland environments are depicted as locations.

desert.presence_definition: Desert environments are depicted as locations.

ocean.definition: Open sea or marine environments are narratively important.
ocean.presence_definition: Open sea or marine environments are depicted as locations.

island.presence_definition: Island environments are depicted as locations.

space_station.definition: An orbital or deep-space station is narratively important.
space_station.presence_definition: An orbital or deep-space station is depicted as a location.

spacecraft.definition: A vehicle traveling through space is narratively important.
spacecraft.presence_definition: A vehicle traveling through space is depicted as a location.

underground.presence_definition: Underground spaces are depicted as locations.

bunker.definition: A protective or military bunker is narratively important.
bunker.presence_definition: A protective or military bunker is depicted as a location.

mansion.definition: A large private residence or estate is narratively important.
mansion.presence_definition: A large private residence or estate is depicted as a location.

home.definition: Domestic living spaces are narratively important.
home.presence_definition: Domestic living spaces are depicted as locations.

school.definition: A primary or secondary school is narratively important.
school.presence_definition: A primary or secondary school is depicted as a location.

university.definition: A university or college environment is narratively important.
university.presence_definition: A university or college environment is depicted as a location.

office.definition: An office workplace is narratively important.
office.presence_definition: An office workplace is depicted as a location.

hospital.definition: A hospital or clinic is narratively important.
hospital.presence_definition: A hospital or clinic is depicted as a location.

restaurant.definition: A restaurant or cafe is narratively important.
restaurant.presence_definition: A restaurant or cafe is depicted as a location.

bar_or_club.definition: A bar, nightclub, or similar nightlife venue is narratively important.
bar_or_club.presence_definition: A bar, nightclub, or similar nightlife venue is depicted as a location.

hotel.definition: A hotel or resort is narratively important.
hotel.presence_definition: A hotel or resort is depicted as a location.

factory.definition: An industrial production site is narratively important.
factory.presence_definition: An industrial production site is depicted as a location.

laboratory.definition: A research or testing laboratory is narratively important.
laboratory.presence_definition: A research or testing laboratory is depicted as a location.

prison.definition: A prison or detention facility is narratively important.
prison.presence_definition: A prison or detention facility is depicted as a location.

salon.definition: A beauty or hair salon is narratively important.
salon.presence_definition: A beauty or hair salon is depicted as a location.

subway.definition: An underground urban rail system is narratively important.
subway.presence_definition: An underground urban rail system is depicted as a location.

airport.presence_definition: An airport is depicted as a location.

amusement_park.definition: An amusement park is narratively important.
amusement_park.presence_definition: An amusement park is depicted as a location.

circus.definition: A circus or carnival is narratively important.
circus.presence_definition: A circus or carnival is depicted as a location.

theater.definition: A theater or performance stage is narratively important.
theater.presence_definition: A theater or performance stage is depicted as a location.

museum.definition: A museum or gallery is narratively important.
museum.presence_definition: A museum or gallery is depicted as a location.

library_or_bookshop.definition: A library or bookshop is narratively important.
library_or_bookshop.presence_definition: A library or bookshop is depicted as a location.

religious_site.definition: A place of worship or religious practice is narratively important.
religious_site.presence_definition: A place of worship or religious practice is depicted as a location.

cemetery.definition: A cemetery or burial ground is narratively important.
cemetery.presence_definition: A cemetery or burial ground is depicted as a location.

plot_velocity.definition: Rate at which consequential plot events occur.

gradual_development.definition: Deliberate accumulation of character, relationships, or tension over time; can coexist with rapid action.

intrigue.definition: Strength of curiosity about what happens or what is concealed.

plot_complexity.definition: Interdependence of events, causes, and plot threads.

interpretive_ambiguity.definition: Extent to which meaning or events support multiple interpretations.

twist_frequency.definition: Recurrence of major reversals or revelations over the work.

twist_impact.definition: Extent to which revelations alter understanding or expectations.

multiple_timelines.definition: Use of distinct temporal strands; not necessarily time travel.

multiple_viewpoints.definition: Distribution of storytelling across distinct character perspectives.

unreliable_narration.definition: Uncertainty created by an unreliable narrator or viewpoint.

unreliable_reality.definition: Uncertainty about which presented events or reality layers are real.

self_reference.definition: Attention to the work's own storytelling or construction.

fourth_wall_breaking.definition: Explicit acknowledgment of the audience or of the work as a presented fiction, including direct address. Voiceover alone is not sufficient.

voiceover.definition: Use of spoken narration over images outside ordinary scene dialogue.

dream_sequences.definition: Use of dreams or hallucinations as presented sequences.

observational_mode.definition: Attention to behavior and environments without strong explanatory or plot intervention.

slice_of_life.definition: Emphasis on ordinary experience rather than extraordinary plot escalation.

exposition_load.definition: Amount of explanatory information the viewer must absorb.

information_withholding.definition: Deliberate delay in supplying information needed to understand events.

educational_intent.definition: Deliberate presentation of factual knowledge for learning.

formal_challenge.definition: Departure from familiar formal conventions that demands adaptation.

homage.definition: Recognizable tributes and references to other works.

pastiche.definition: Imitation or combination of recognizable artistic styles.

didacticism.definition: How explicitly the work states, teaches or argues a message; independent of intellectual stimulation or whether the viewer agrees.

confined_setting.definition: Concentration of the work within a single location or tightly bounded connected spaces; distinct from small cast, low budget or confinement as a plot event.

real_time.definition: Elapsed story time closely tracks presentation time; not simply fast plotting.

vignette_structure.definition: Discrete short episodes, scenes or chapters form the work; distinguish from multiple timelines.

narrativity.definition: A developing sequence of causally or temporally linked events organizes the work; 0 indicates non-narrative form, not failure or low quality.

personal.definition: Consequences for an individual's life, identity, or goals.

relationship.definition: Consequences for a central relationship or small social unit.

community.definition: Consequences for a locality or community.

societal.definition: Consequences for institutions, a society, or civilization.

planetary.definition: Consequences extending to a planet or humanity as a whole.

cosmic.definition: Consequences extending beyond planetary life to cosmic reality.

urgency.definition: Time pressure on consequential decisions or events.

density.definition: Amount of spoken dialogue relative to the work's running time.

dependence.definition: Importance of understanding dialogue to follow the work.

overlap.definition: Use of simultaneous or overlapping speech.

naturalistic_delivery.definition: Conversational delivery resembling spontaneous everyday speech.

theatrical_delivery.definition: Heightened, rhetorical, or explicitly performative speech.

multilingual_exchange.definition: Use of multiple languages within the work; factual languages are catalog data.

cyberpunk.definition: High technology combined with alienation, social stratification, or countercultural urban imagery.

steampunk.definition: Retro-industrial speculative imagery drawing on steam-age technology.

gothic.definition: Ominous, decaying, or romantically macabre visual atmosphere.

noir.definition: Shadowed, morally uneasy visual and atmospheric treatment, independently of crime plotting.

retro.definition: Deliberately retrospective visual or sonic styling; not merely an older release.

minimalism.definition: Reduction of visual, sonic, or formal elements.

stylization.definition: Departure from naturalistic presentation through a distinctive audiovisual treatment.

surrealism.definition: Dreamlike or illogical relationships in presented images and events.

psychedelia.definition: Hallucinatory, distorted, or perceptually altered sensory treatment.

grotesquerie.definition: Emphasis on distorted, repulsive, or biologically unsettling forms.

camp.definition: Theatrical excess and conspicuous artifice with an invitation to enjoy that excess.

ironic_distance.definition: Presentation that invites distance from its apparent surface meaning.

intimacy.definition: Presentation fostering closeness to characters' private experience.

spectacle.definition: Emphasis on impressive scale, effects, and set pieces.

immersion.definition: Strength of the sensory sense of inhabiting the work's world.

lyricism.definition: Poetic, associative presentation through image, language, sound or rhythm; not a synonym for slow pacing.

transgression.definition: Perceptible aesthetic treatment that deliberately challenges taboos or conventions; do not infer a creator's private intent or equate explicit content alone with transgression.

muted_palette.definition: Use of restrained or desaturated colors.

scoring_contract.intermediate_values: Integers between anchors interpolate within the same rubric. Do not imply measured precision beyond evidence.

statuses.numeric: A 0–10 integer is assessed; null means unknown/unassessed. Movie show-only fields are inapplicable and null.
statuses.presence: Use the explicit present/absent/unknown states; never collapse unknown into absence.

scoring_contract.omission: All declared keys are required. Missing keys are contract failures, not zeros or implicit negatives.
scoring_contract.confidence: No calibrated confidence or per-field evidence object is requested. Record assessment_basis honestly; controller-owned source/run records retain actual provenance.
scoring_contract.scope: Every assessment belongs to an explicit movie, whole-show, season, or episode scope with an as-of date and coverage statement.

intensity.10: Exceptionally strong or pervasive in the defined scope.
intensity.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

centrality.0: No narrative importance. The content may be absent or present without a meaningful role; use content_presence separately where covered. Zero alone never certifies absence.
centrality.10: Defining focus; removing it fundamentally changes the work.
centrality.1: Supported, very minor narrative importance; occurrence alone is insufficient. Zero means no narrative importance, not certified absence.

membership.0: Does not use the genre conventions.
membership.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

prominence.8: Prominent across much of the scope.
prominence.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

frequency.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

quality.10: Exceptional execution. Absence is not a zero-quality score.
quality.1: Very unsuccessful execution; not a default for unknown quality or absent craft.

suitability.0: Very poor fit under the stated assumptions.
suitability.10: Exceptionally strong fit. Not a universal audience verdict.

separate_dimensions: Genre membership is not subject presence.
Release era is not setting era.
Production origin is not depicted culture or influence.
Intended audience is not age suitability.
Aesthetic appearance does not establish production technique.
Content presence is not narrative importance: a present detail can have centrality zero. Unknown presence and unknown applicability remain explicit.
scoring_contract.advisory_absence: An absent advisory requires sufficient coverage of the relevant scope and version. Do not turn synopsis silence into absence.
scoring_contract.series_policy: Movie scopes require null for every show-only numeric field and facet. Whole-show assessments name covered seasons; no claims about unassessed later releases.

storytelling.chronology.definition: Substantial presentation patterns within scope; select every pattern actually used. Chronological and reverse-chronological strands can coexist. Occasional memories do not establish interleaved timelines; a repeated time loop alone is not reverse chronology. Non-temporal applies to substantial passages not organized by story time.

storytelling.retelling_structure.definition: Ways substantially the same events are presented again from different accounts. Parallel storylines alone do not qualify. Complementary accounts add information; conflicting accounts disagree. Select both when both occur; [] when assessed with neither.

storytelling.tone_progression.definition: Substantial tone patterns within scope, not an exact timeline or a claim about every episode. Select multiple directions if different arcs use them. Broadly stable applies to substantial stable stretches; alternating tones means repeated switching. Comedy and horror blended throughout do not alone establish comic_to_horror.

characters.competence_basis.definition: How focal characters' demonstrated skill is established. These are whole-work categories, not claims that all tags describe the same person. Do not equate intelligence with competence.

presentation.narration_sources.definition: Sources of narration or explanatory speech, excluding ordinary dialogue. First-person character narration does not imply direct audience address. Source recordings are retained historical/archival speech rather than newly added explanation.

presentation.jump_scares.definition: Abrupt audiovisual events deliberately staged to startle. General fear, loudness or sustained tension alone is not a jump scare.

presentation.jump_scare_modalities.definition: Modalities used by actual jump scares, independently of sound-design prominence. Empty only when assessed absent; null when undetermined.

presentation.laugh_track.definition: Recorded or live audience laughter included in the soundtrack; ordinary characters laughing is excluded.

presentation.sustained_screaming.definition: Extended or repeatedly sustained screaming in the soundtrack, distinct from an isolated shout or startle.

ending.post_credits_function.definition: Functions of scenes during or after credits within the assessed edition. Select all that apply, including multiple functions in one scene. [] means no qualifying scene/functions; null means undetermined. A comic tag need not reopen a threat.

series.case_resolution_pattern.definition: Recurring case/problem resolution patterns in the assessed episodes. Select all substantial patterns; [] when there is no case/problem structure. Not cancellation status, ending quality or a promise about unseen seasons.

series.character_continuity.definition: Substantial continuity patterns for character relationships/development across the assessed episodes. Resetting some strands and developing others can coexist. Independently assessed from case resolution.

world_context.eras.definition: Substantial depicted story eras, not production dates. A brief mention or prop does not establish a setting. Ancient/medieval are broad temporal labels, not a claim that all societies share one historical periodization.

world_context.relative_periods.definition: Substantial story periods relative to the title's original release, not today. Multiple selections describe the work overall, without pairing each period to an event.

world_context.reality_layers.definition: Kinds of depicted reality that matter to the work. Physical staged reality (e.g. an elaborate set) is distinct from a digital simulation or virtual reality.

world_context.environmental_obstacles.definition: Environmental conditions that materially impede action or survival. Scenic weather alone does not qualify; these tags do not identify who is obstructed or when.

seasonal.depicted_seasons.definition: Substantial seasons depicted, based on the setting's local climate/calendar. Release month and viewing associations are insufficient.

seasonal.depicted_holidays.definition: Named celebrations actually depicted or materially organizing the story. This bounded vocabulary is not exhaustive; do not invent a new label for an unlisted tradition.

cultural.movements_and_traditions.definition: Established artistic affiliation or substantial recognizable stylistic tradition. Country, language, slow pacing or production date alone is insufficient. This list is bounded; unlisted traditions require a future schema revision, not a guessed synonym.

cultural.depicted_contexts.definition: Social/cultural experiences substantially depicted, independently of the production industry or an actor's identity. Diaspora and indigenous contexts require established depiction, not inference from appearance.

representation.established_protagonist_t.definition: Explicitly established traits of one or more protagonists/co-protagonists. Whole-work set: selections need not describe the same person. Never infer from an actor's identity, appearance, name or a viewer stereotype.

format_facts.production_method.definition: Substantial production methods used. Select both for live-action/animation combinations; ordinary CGI visual effects alone do not make a live-action work animated.

format_facts.narrative_mode.definition: Modes used in substantial passages; select fiction and nonfiction for an explicit hybrid. A fictional mockumentary is fiction, not nonfiction merely because it imitates a documentary.

format_facts.series_structure.definition: Show formats used within scope. Limited describes a deliberately bounded run and can coexist with episodic, serialized or anthology structure. Not current release/cancellation status.

format_facts.color_process.definition: Substantial color presentation modes in the assessed edition. Select color and black_and_white if both occur; tinting can coexist with an underlying monochrome image.

format_facts.adaptation_type.definition: Source-material types contributing substantially. Multiple sources may coexist; original refers to substantial independently originated material, not every small adaptation change. Do not invent source-work identifiers.

format_facts.factual_basis.definition: Relationships to real people/events within scope; multiple selections may apply. Disputed is supported factual controversy, not the model being unsure. No selection certifies accuracy.

format_facts.animation_techniques.definition: Animation techniques actually used, not creatures depicted. Select each substantial technique instead of a generic mixed tag.

format_facts.presentation_modes.definition: Observable presentation modes, not audience approval.

format_facts.documentary_devices.definition: Devices used in documentary-style presentation, including fictional mockumentary. Voiceover origin is captured separately.

format_facts.capture_media.definition: Known original capture media, never inferred from a digital streaming release or merely simulated grain. Select each known medium. Null when undetermined; do not guess components from a mixed-format label.

format_facts.work_relation_types.definition: Known relation types to other works; these tags do not resolve target works or establish influence from resemblance alone.

format_facts.anime_tradition.definition: Affiliation with the anime production/artistic tradition; animation alone is insufficient.

format_facts.silent_or_intertitles.definition: Principally silent-film/intertitle presentation, not simply sparse dialogue.

format_facts.single_take_presentation.definition: Whole work presented as one continuous take, real or simulated; an isolated long take is insufficient.

format_facts.real_time_presentation.definition: Main narrative is presented approximately in real elapsed time; not merely rapid plot events.

format_facts.post_credits_scene_present.definition: A scene during/after credits in this edition, not ordinary credit text.

format_facts.alternate_endings_present.definition: Known alternative endings for this title/edition; do not invent them from narrative ambiguity.

attributes_value_contract.numeric: 0–10 integer or null. Null means unknown/unassessed; show-only movie values are inapplicable and must be null.
attributes_value_contract.presence: present/absent/unknown. Never derive absence from zero or silence. These are model assessments, not verified exclusion guarantees.
attributes_value_contract.categorical: Every categorical facet is a multi-select array of distinct supported choices, or null when undetermined. [] means assessed with no listed category identified. Binary facts and mutually exclusive presence states remain scalar. Never use mixed/both/none sentinels in a multi-select list.
attributes_value_contract.combinations: All fields refer to the same title scope, but independent tags need not refer to the same character, event, season or scene.
attributes_value_contract.prose: No prose field participates in this data contract. Optional existing display descriptions remain outside matching attributes.
